findings.issue: The REQ-SAG-0618 command `! cargo tree -p sc-agent-types -e normal | grep -qE '...(sha2|uuid) v[0-9]'` scans the transitive tree. If sc-sha itself depends on sha2, that check cannot pass even when the plan is followed. This depends on the owner-gated D0 outcome, so it is a risk, not a proven failure. REQ-SAG-0618 and architecture.md:1575 also say sha2/uuid are removed from the workspace unconditionally, while D2 says 'when nothing else uses them' (the Cargo.lock part). Today sha2 and uuid are used only by sc-agent-types and sc-ai (Cargo.toml grep).
findings.required_correction: Make the command check direct dependencies (`cargo tree -p sc-agent-types -e normal --depth 1`) and match 'removed from the workspace' to 'no workspace manifest lists them'. Do not decide the sc-sha gate.
